narratives.title: Geopolitical Escalation Risk-Off
narratives.summary: Capital is fleeing risk assets as multi-front conflicts (Iran, Israel, Ukraine) escalate beyond controlled tit-for-tat, with credible threats to energy chokepoints like Hormuz. The market consensus underestimates the persistence and structural nature of these disruptions, driving flows into safe havens and commodities.
narratives.trade_implication: Long WTI crude oil and short S&P 500 futures; overweight gold and short-dated US Treasuries.

narratives.title: Energy Supply Disruption Premium
narratives.summary: Capital is pricing in a sustained oil supply shock from the Hormuz blockade and SPR releases, which are actually bullish signals of government concern. The EIA's extended blockade timeline through Q3 2026 and Kuwait's pipeline bypass discussions confirm structural tightness, not transient noise.
narratives.trade_implication: Long WTI and Brent futures; long energy sector equities and short consumer discretionary.

narratives.title: Crypto as Macro Risk Proxy
narratives.summary: Bitcoin's crash mirrors broad risk-off moves, not crypto-specific weakness, as institutional de-risking dominates. Whales and MicroStrategy buying the dip suggest underlying accumulation, but capital flows are currently driven by macro fear rather than fundamental conviction.
narratives.trade_implication: Short BTC futures or long put spreads; wait for geopolitical de-escalation before re-entering long positions.
